comment: brief-emi-2 R-emi2-1. uv, a pinned Python and a hash-locked EMerge, all inside the home: no system Python is read or changed. The lock lines are tools/EmergeLock/make_locks.py's output. brief-emi-3: its optional tail builds the faster macOS sparse solver from a pinned commit whenever the command line tools are installed, now or later. brief-emi-9: a second optional group builds EMerge's GPU sparse solver from a pinned commit whenever a Rust toolchain is found as well; the bootstrap is what Settings' Enable GPU solving fetches for that one build when none is.
layoutNote: The environment's python is a link to the interpreter by absolute path, and its pyvenv.cfg names that interpreter's folder the same way (measured on macOS arm64), so the home cannot be renamed into place and is built where it stays.

sources.checksumNote: uv 0.12.24 checks the Python 3.13.16 archive it downloads against the SHA-256 it carries for that build
every package is pinned to an exact version and checked against the SHA-256 hashes in requirements.lock, which this recipe writes; uv refuses a file whose hash is not listed

sources.fetchedBy: git (only with the command line tools)
sources.checksumNote: a git fetch of commit 47ad46880c3d26df126943ecfffb68864b1875d4, checked against that commit after the fetch; built on this machine and never redistributed

sources.fetchedBy: git (only with the command line tools and a Rust toolchain)
sources.checksumNote: a git fetch of commit a178949d00f17bcacdcfff1a0ff5f92467aa817d, checked against that commit after the fetch; its Rust dependencies are the ones its Cargo.lock pins, which cargo checks against their SHA-256 (--locked); built on this machine and never redistributed

bootstrap.comment: brief-emi-9 R-emi9-2b. Rust's official installer at a pinned version, told where to put everything (RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_HOME) and not to touch the user's shell (--no-modify-path): the user's own PATH, profile and any Rust they install later are untouched. circuitRF deletes the folder after the build, whatever happened.
bootstrap.name: Rust's minimal toolchain

sources.checksumNote: rustup 1.29.2 checks each component of Rust 1.98.1 it downloads against the SHA-256 in that release's manifest

steps.name: Download Rust's installer (rustup 1.29.2)
Make Rust's installer runnable
Install Rust 1.98.1's minimal toolchain into the EMerge home

notes: Rust is free software under the MIT and Apache 2.0 licences; circuitRF uses it for this one build and then deletes it.

measured.source: rustup 1.29.2 installing Rust 1.98.1's minimal profile on an M4, 2026-10-22: 28 s for 99 MB (the 11 MB installer and 88 MB of components), 447 MB on disk until it is deleted

consentNotes: EMerge is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 2 or later, and so is Gmsh, which it meshes with; circuitRF starts them as separate programs and distributes neither.
The faster sparse solver it builds on this machine declares the MIT licence; circuitRF builds it here from its upstream source and distributes nothing.

The GPU sparse solver it builds when a Rust toolchain is present is under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or later; circuitRF builds it here from its upstream source, EMerge runs it in its own process, and circuitRF distributes nothing.

Unpack uv
Install Python 3.13.16
steps.comment: --no-bin and --no-registry keep uv from adding a python command to ~/.local/bin or registering the interpreter with Windows: the interpreter lives in the home and nowhere else.

steps.name: Create the Python environment
Write the locked requirements
lines: # Written by circuitRF's install assistant from recipe ${recipeId}: EMerge and every package it needs, each at

steps.name: Install EMerge 3.0.0b3
steps.comment: --require-hashes refuses any file the lock does not name; --no-build refuses anything that would compile; --compile-bytecode spends the start-up a first run would otherwise pay.

steps.name: Check that EMerge imports
steps.comment: -I: the user's PYTHONPATH and site-packages play no part. A broken environment fails here, not at the first run.

steps.name: Clear uv's download cache
steps.comment: The cache roughly doubles the home's size and nothing reads it again.

steps.name: Fetch the faster sparse solver's source
steps.comment: brief-emi-3 R-emi3-2b. init, fetch one commit and check it out: each step can run again over what an interrupted attempt left, which a clone cannot. /usr/bin/git is only asked once the prerequisite says the tools are there; asked before, it opens the command line tools' installer instead of answering.

steps.name: Fetch commit 47ad468 of the faster sparse solver
Check out the faster sparse solver's source
Check the faster sparse solver's commit
Write the locked build requirements
lines: # Written by circuitRF's install assistant from recipe ${recipeId}: what building the faster sparse solver needs,
# at an exact version with the SHA-256 of its one file. Its build is otherwise a single C file, compiled by clang.

steps.name: Install the build requirements
Build and install the faster sparse solver
steps.comment: --no-build-isolation: the build uses the hash-locked setuptools above rather than fetching whatever is newest; --no-deps: what it needs is already in the environment. Measured: 1 s on an M4.

steps.name: Check that EMerge finds the faster sparse solver
arguments: from emerge._emerge import solver as s; print(s._AASDS_AVAILABLE)
steps.comment: EMerge imports it inside a try and quietly falls back when the library does not load, so this is the step that says whether the build worked.

steps.name: Clear uv's download cache again
Fetch the GPU sparse solver's source
steps.comment: brief-emi-9 R-emi9-2. As the faster sparse solver's: init, fetch one commit, check it out, check the commit.

# Python, at an exact version with the SHA-256 of its one file. The rest of its build is Rust, pinned by its Cargo.lock.

steps.name: Install the GPU solver's build requirements
Build and install the GPU sparse solver
steps.comment: The build tool finds cargo ONLY on PATH (a GUI app's PATH has no ~/.cargo/bin), so the step's PATH starts with the folder the prerequisite found it in. --no-build-isolation with the hash-locked build tool above, and MATURIN_NO_INSTALL_RUST in the recipe's environment: an isolated build fetches whatever is newest, and with no cargo on PATH it downloads a whole Rust toolchain into the user's cache folder unasked (measured: 507 MB). --locked builds exactly what Cargo.lock pins. Measured: 17 s on an M4.

steps.name: Check that EMerge finds the GPU sparse solver
arguments: from emerge._emerge import solver as s; print(s._SPARTA_AVAILABLE)
steps.comment: EMerge imports it inside a try, and refuses one older than 0.2.0, quietly either way.

steps.name: Clear uv's download cache after the GPU build

measured.source: circuitRF's own install, macOS 27.0 on an M4, 2026-10-21: 137 s and 1.02 GB after uv's cache was cleared (906 MB environment, 71 MB Python, 28 MB uv); the probe then answered EMerge 3.0.0b2, Python 3.13.16, Gmsh 4.15.2, baseline sparse solver. Re-pinned to 3.0.0b3 on 2026-10-22, whose wheel changes no solver code; its install with both optional groups built took 107 s and 1.24 GB, as 3.0.0b2's did
